questions.question: What are the four stages of the CIRO approach?
questions.solution_html: • What are the four stages of the CIRO approach? Ans: The four stages of the CIRO approach are Context, Input, Reaction, and Outcome. It evaluates training by analyzing organizational needs (Context), training design (Input), participant feedback (Reaction), and the resulting behavioral and performance changes or outcomes in the workplace.

questions.question: Why is training typically shorter in duration than development?
questions.solution_html: • Why is training typically shorter in duration than development? Ans: Training is typically shorter because it focuses on specific skills or tasks needed immediately for a job. Development, however, is broader and long-term, aimed at overall growth, leadership, and future roles, requiring more time and continuous learning efforts.
